faq_items.question: What is a goal planner printable?
faq_items.answer: A goal planner printable is a fill-in sheet that turns broad resolutions into a workable plan. It sorts your goals by life area, breaks each into quarterly milestones and a monthly focus, and includes a habit tracker so you can mark the daily actions that move each goal forward.

faq_items.question: How many goals should I set for the year?
faq_items.answer: Choose just two or three goals to lead the year, not one per category. A short list keeps your focus from being shredded across a dozen competing priorities. Capture every other idea as a "someday" note so it is recorded, then point this year's energy at the few that matter most.

faq_items.question: What is the best way to break down a yearly goal?
faq_items.answer: Work backward from the finish line. Split a yearly goal into a quarterly milestone, then a monthly focus, then a weekly action. Saving $1,000, for example, becomes about $250 a quarter, $85 a month, and $20 a week, small enough to start today and easy to check your pace against.

faq_items.question: Why do most goal planners stop working by February?
faq_items.answer: Most planners fail because people set too many goals and never revisit them. A dozen goals split your attention until none moves, and a planner left in a drawer might as well be blank. Capping your list and scheduling a monthly review are what keep a plan alive past February.

faq_items.question: Do I need to print a new goal planner every month?
faq_items.answer: You do not have to. Many people slip the sheet into a sheet protector and mark it with a dry-erase marker, wiping the habit tracker clean at the start of each month. Others reprint monthly to keep a written record of their progress. Either approach works, pick whichever you will actually maintain.
